posts.name: joahprivette
posts.cooked:
Now that it is official I want to share my feelings on ending the SotM card game.

Straight to the meat of it; I feel that ending this line is not only premature but also a heavy dose of "head in the sand ". None of their games are working* and this newest Kickstarter is not the savior either. I understand not relying on your laurels but I feel they are blindly jumping off a cliff at this point. There are literally a dozen new things that can be done with SotM card game and that universe (beside the atrocious Tactics) and yet if those plans are in the works they are making us(long time GTG fans) feel like we are part of a sinking ship in the meantime. 

I was hoping Dice Hate Me would be the turnaround but really their portfolio is worst of all. Especially if you take into account their bestselling game, VivaJava, will see its 4 YEAR anniversary (most of that was Out of Stock) before a second edition makes it to market. The dice version doesn't even have a reprint announced yet!! Then there is the newest KS which may or may not fund but if it does it will be just barley (and I really doubt that it will). All and all it just seems like a bad time to end your biggest presence in the board game scene and I really hope they have better marketing plans in the future than Great and Better....

Not a hater just a concerned fan for non Asmodee publishers 

-JP

 

*working - Selling well past publication cost and attracting many new players to your brand.

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
Spiff:

I agree it seems like an odd (possibly disastrous) choice to stop the most successful thing you’ve got … I guess we just have to hope that they can produce a new winner so they can keep making money

I highly doubt that they’d stop selling the Sentinels core game, so it will still be making them money. Heck, if they simply re-issued what they have with errata changes and new art bells and whistles, they’d inject themselves right onto store shelves again and lots of current owners would re-buy everything.

From their perspective, they may be looking at how much money Sentinels makes over time, whether expansions are selling progressively more or less than previous ones, and how well the base game does after all this time. They are probably also looking at how to get their audience to grow, not just how to keep the one they have. Put another way: Dominion expansions are still coming out…but are we buying them as much any more? I’m not.

Another thing that doesn’t necessarily go away with the end of Sentinels’ story is the game mechanic. There’s absolutely no reason why they can’t repurpose or modify the mechanic for new games. Get a posse to go fight outlaws in the old west? Go questing through a dungeon? Overthrow a tyrannical space empire? Board and pirate merchantmen on the high seas? All could easily fit into the hero/villain/environment deck structure. And all could easily have as big a pile of lore as Sentinels.

I bet, in the end, Christopher and Adam may just want to try some new things. They may feel like additional Sentinels expansions are going to come out more and more gimmicky in an effort to be distinct from what already exists. They might have some other ideas they want to devote their time to.

I share your apprehension a little, as I haven’t seen >G penetrate into several of my local game stores and I hope they can put out new things as high-caliber as Sentinels. I’m looking forward to Spirit Island, but that will be something entirely new - which comes with its own apprehension. In the end the reason I’m most sad to see the end of the Sentinels story is just that I like it and I’m sorry to see it go. But it’s always going to be here on my game shelf, and those boxes are filled with a LOT of combinations. If it’s going to end, due to whatever business case factors that I can’t see, I’d rather it do so in a planned, graceful way. And I’d much rather a planned ending than a continuation as a tent-pole property that becomes more and more likely to included big misses as it does hits (probably none of which will be as much a hit as the original). Down that road lies Jar-Jar Binks. Let’s not wish the same fate on Thiago!

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
I'm a firm believer that stories have to end. I mean, look at the repetitive drudgery and contrived bull that is the mainstream comics scene. The stories don't end -- they just get rebooted and retreaded every handful of years. You get invested in a storyline, then COSMIC BULLSHIT and suddenly all your favorite stories are no longer in continuity, characters are changed so you don't recognize them, and stupid things like selling a marriage to satan happen.

I'd much, much rather see any story I like come to a proper conclusion than have it languish on and on.

Ending Sentinels on a high note is ballsy and I support it wholeheartedly.

posts.name: lynkfox
posts.cooked:
my opinion is just because the story of this version of Sentinels is done doesn't mean the product isnt. I don't think that the release of new expansions is what is keeping GtG afloat - if that were true, thats a bad business model too, searching for a new cash cow to keep going. 

 

Some things i see as a possibility

 

1) New Core set - with updated artwork to Adam's new style/experience, possibly a reworking of a few of the core heroes decks to be more in line with the power levels some of the newer heroes have shown.  - I would totally rebuy the coreset if Adam updated all the artwork to his new levels of awesomeness.

2) Play. Power. Draw and cooperative decks vrs a automated deck mechanics being reused in a new game with a new setting. A new story to tell, that isnt Sentinel Comics but still has Christopher's storytelling behind it.

3) and least likely in my eyes, Sentinels 2.0 - as a new story (after tactics? between Sentinels 1.0 and Tactics?) or in an alternate universe (see Legacy Setback as it's own deck? or the heroes from that one card in La Capitan Villains deck?)

 

Now I don't have any idea of the finances behind this, but the games are still selling - evidence of the reprints, and that seems to be a viable strategy. Just cause this is the final expansion doesn't mean that no one can buy the game anymore, or that they'll stop reprinting them. Dice Hate Me games may not be as popular here on the forums, but that I view as the 20/80 syndrome of the internet, and DHMG was viable before GtG merged with them. I don't feel like that was a 'we'll save you!' from either side fo the merger, but rather they saw they could reach more together and help support each other.

 

I also see a lot of oppertunities for new products with just the 3 above options (who knows, Mini expansions could still be a thing! I'd love a villain deck for Heartbreaker or a hero deck for ... well anyone!)  and really don't think that just cause they aren't going to print new material with this specific story doesn't mean that its a financial ending to the product line.  

 

BUT... i'm a courier, chef, and game player. Not a financial officer.  Take what I say with a grain of salt.

posts.name: TheSoundOfTrees
posts.cooked:
The Multiverse story line is ending -  that's all.

What I mean is that I think that their plan has come to fruition, the story they wanted to tell has come to an end. It does not mean that they will never ever again give us a new expansion - or variation - on SotM. It will just be another story, and it is not (at least officially) planned for now.

I an convinced that it is not the last time we will hear of our beloved game - there are too many mysteries left unsolved ( Why are the Parsons so special ? What about the future Visionary is from ? Why is Haka immortal ? Who is CON?) and I doubt OblivAeon will give an answer to all of them. Knowing Christopher, I would bet it will gives us MORE mysteries

There are too many possible expansions,or even variants, of the game, for them not to be published someday. But not aas part of the main line - and not before they have had enough time to plan a good product, and not a purely commercial "yet another expansion". This not Carcassone

But I would not be surprised if we someday saw a new stand alone box about heroes and villains from the past ( Black Fist and friends !),or maybe the story of sentinels comics after tactics. Or small box sets about FILTER, RevoCorp, the future Visionary is from, etc. Compatible with SotM, maybe - but not part of the main story. At least it is what I hope they plan to do someday

And it is not counting other games set in the same universe. A "Freedom Five" campaign boardgame would make my day.

I agree that from a creative standpoint, the story should end.  I prefer my stories to have beginnings, middles, and ends, just like everyone (and I also agree that there are too many stories out there which never do end).  But from a business standpoint, voluntarily ending updates to your hit product without another to take its place is counter-intuitive to me.

I love the idea of using the core mechanic to tell other stories.  A rebooted GSF "powered by the SotM" engine would have an easy shot at my wallet.

Counter-argument: Think about how well Settlers of Catan core game sells vs. all of the expansions.  Ending Sentinels just means no more expansions, it does not mean stopping publishing of the game and the existing expansions.  In fact, having it be complete might help them improve their ability to market the core game to new audiences (I think about the breakthrough in sales that Looney Labs got after managing to get Fluxx into Target).

Yeah, I wouldn't be surprised to see a "Complete Set" box become available, with new goodies and feelies (like, say, a copy of the comic book on the website).
